rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A formula that passes the check can still have the wrong numerical factor.  ·  You cannot derive a law from dimensions if you omit a quantity that matters.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The pendulum result assumes small swings and no dependence on mass.  ·  A formula with both g and a spring constant may need an extra argument.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Dimensional analysis is used in three ways. It checks whether an equation could be right. It converts a numerical value from one unit system to another. It suggests the form of a relation when the relevant quantities are known.  ·  To find a form, write the unknown as a product of powers of the chosen quantities, then equate the powers of M, L and T on both sides. The solution of those three equations gives the powers.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Unit conversion is not the same task as finding a new law.  ·  Adding quantities of different dimensions is rejected, even if the numbers look similar.

rows.label: Derivation

rows.text: Assume the period of a simple pendulum depends on length l and g as T = k l^a g^b. Find a and b.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The time period of a simple pendulum is assumed to depend on its length and on g, and not on the mass, when the amplitude is small. Matching dimensions then gives T proportional to the square root of l/g.  ·  The method cannot produce the 2π in that pendulum formula. Any dimensionless constant is invisible. An experiment, or a full derivation, has to supply it.  ·  The method also fails if a needed quantity is left out of the assumption, or if too many quantities are included. With more than three unknown powers and only M, L and T, the powers are not fixed uniquely.

rows.text: Too many variables  ·  Cannot find a dimensionless factor.  ·  Uses of Dimensional Analysis & Its Limitations is based on fundamental principles.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions accept only dimensionless inputs. Dimensional analysis will reject a formula that puts a length alone inside a sine.
